text:
mike: Heads up — saw a burst of ECC correctable errors on us-west-2 gpu-pool-4 starting ~10:03. Alerts flooded the channel. Concentrated on hosts gpu-n1, gpu-n7, gpu-n9. Correctable_count jumped from ~2/min to ~120/min for those cards.
lara: link to the grafana? :eyes:
mike: grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/GPUECC/gpu-ecc-overview?orgId=1&var-cluster=us-west-2
mike: PromQL I used: `sum by(card) (increase(nv_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[5m]))` — shows the three cards standing out.
jeff: Any Xid/unrecoverable errors or just correctables?
mike: Mostly correctables. A couple of kernel warnings with Xid 31 on gpu-n9 around 10:08 but no immediate machine reboot.
natasha: Do we have an auto-drain policy that would've triggered?
ops-bot: alert: GPU_ECC_BURST - gpu-pool-4 - 1773501234 - severity:warning
lara: Current auto-drain is pretty blunt: drain after 500 correctable errors in 5m OR 3 uncorrectable Xid. That would probably over-trigger on these short bursts.
jeff: Could be noisy sensor or actual memory degradation. We should distinguish short bursts vs sustained degradation.
lara: Proposal: new heuristic — detect "rate-bursts" and soft-quarantine first.
lara: If increase( nv_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[3m]) > 200 AND at least 2 cards on the same host exceed that, then mark host as `soft-drained` (stop new scheduling, keep existing jobs running) and run diagnostics. If condition persists for additional 10m or uncorrectable Xid appears => escalate to hard-drain and machine-replace workflow.
mike: Sketch of automation + alert config:
```
- alert: GPU_ECC_RATE_BURST
  expr: max by(host) (sum by(card)(increase(nv_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[3m]))) > 200
  for: 0m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    runbook: https://runbook.internal/gpu-ecc-rateburst
```
Then Alertmanager routes warning to `ecc-bursts` webhook which triggers an orchestration lambda that:
  1) checks host.metadata (skip if `critical_customer=true`)
  2) marks host as soft-drained: `fleetctl set-host --no-schedule host` (no eviction)
  3) runs `ssh host sudo /usr/local/bin/gpu-diagnose --ecc --memtest 10m`
  4) if errors persist for >10m or any Xid uncorrectable => `fleetctl drain host --evict` and create replace ticket.
jeff: Two add-ons: 1) normalize by workload intensity (a training job can legitimately produce bursts); consider a metric like `correctable_per_gpu_min / running_batch_jobs` to avoid false positives. 2) Add a cooldown so we don't take > N% of pool offline in 30m.
natasha: Important: for Dedicated customers we can't auto-evict without manual approval. Add tag check `host.metadata.billing_tier=dedicated` and require human confirm for hard-drain.
lara: Also prefer draining within the same AZ to avoid cross-AZ network/cost churn. If forced to replace, try to keep replacements in same AZ.
jeff: Test plan: replay last 6 months of metrics in staging with synthetic ECC injection. Run the automation against `pool-staging` and assert we don't exceed 10% capacity loss and no false hard-drains.
mike: I'll draft a runbook PR with the thresholds, playbook steps, and diagnostics output examples. For the immediate incident I'll mute the noisy alert for 1h to reduce pager fatigue and run diagnostics on gpu-n9.
ops-bot: action: created issue https://tracker.internal/RED-EE-512 - "ecc-rateburst-detect-and-heuristics" and muted alert GPU_ECC_BURST for 1h
sre-oncall: Acknowledged. I'm standing by for diag output. If we get uncorrectable Xid escalate to paging.
natasha: Thanks — assume ownership of the PR with me and jeff for staging tests. Ping if any Xid shows up. :thumbsup:
